t:
Section 9 of the South Pacific Tuna Act of 1988 (16 U.S.C. 973g) is amended by adding at the end thereof the following:


“(h) 
Notwithstanding the requirements of—

“(1) 
section 1 of the Act of August 26, 1983 (97 Stat. 587; 46 U.S.C. 12108);


“(2) 
the general permit issued on December 1, 1980, to the American Tunaboat Association under section 104(h)(1) of the Marine Mammal Protection Act (16 U.S.C. 1374(h)(1)); and



“(3) 

sections 104(h)(2) and 306(a) of the Marine Mammal Protection Act (16 U.S.C. 1374(h)(2) and 1416(a))—
any vessel documented under the laws of the United States as of the date of enactment of the Fisheries Act of 1995 for which a license has been issued under subsection (a) may fish for tuna in the Treaty Area, including those waters subject to the jurisdiction of the United States in accordance with international law, subject to the provisions of the treaty and this Act, provided that no such vessel fishing in the Treaty Area intentionally deploys a purse seine net to encircle any dolphin or other marine mammal in the course of fishing under the provisions of the Treaty or this Act.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to a general permit issued to the American Tunaboat Association and to licensed vessels show outside-party involvement. But these are past permits and licenses, which the definition excludes, and the section simply grants a substantive authorization to fish subject to a dolphin-encirclement condition. It provides no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government.
fable.s: any vessel documented under the laws of the United States as of the date of enactment of the Fisheries Act of 1995 for which a license has been issued under subsection (a) may fish for tuna in the Treaty Area

qwen_block.w: This section grants a specific exemption from certain regulatory requirements (such as general permits) to vessels that already hold a license. It defines the scope of fishing rights and prohibitions (e.g., no intentional encircling of dolphins) but does not establish a process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The mention of the 'American Tunaboat Association' is in the context of a pre-existing permit being overridden, not a new participatory mechanism.
qwen_block.s: any vessel documented under the laws of the United States as of the date of enactment of the Fisheries Act of 1995 for which a license has been issued under subsection (a) may fish for tuna in the Treaty Area

opus.w: This section only lets licensed U.S. vessels fish for tuna in the Treaty Area despite certain other legal requirements, and it bars them from intentionally encircling dolphins. The mentions of a general permit to the American Tunaboat Association and of vessel licenses could look like outside involvement. But licenses and permits are applications, which the definition excludes, and the 1980 permit is a past event rather than a future process. No outside party is consulted or given a say before any federal decision.
opus.s: any vessel documented under the laws of the United States as of the date of enactment of the Fisheries Act of 1995 for which a license has been issued under subsection (a) may fish for tuna in the Treaty Area
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation because it mentions a general permit issued to the American Tunaboat Association, an outside group, and licenses issued to vessels. That fails because licenses and permits are applications, not participation. The 1980 permit is also a past event. Nothing in the section sets up consultation, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants permission to specific vessels to fish in a certain area, subject to existing licenses and treaty provisions. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or include non-federal members in an advisory body before making a decision. The reference to the American Tunaboat Association is merely citing an existing permit, not establishing a new participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: any vessel documented under the laws of the United States as of the date of enactment of the Fisheries Act of 1995 for which a license has been issued under subsection (a) may fish for tuna in the Treaty Area
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to the "American Tunaboat Association" or the general regulatory context implies participation. However, the text itself only grants a fishing license/permission to vessels and sets a prohibition on fishing methods. It does not describe a process where the government consults with outsiders, holds a public hearing, or creates an advisory body with outside members before making a decision. The mention of the Association is merely referencing an existing permit, not establishing a new participatory mechanism in this section.
